review_notes: Read the whole target file and the simp-tagged parent lemmas in CentralPolynomialSimplex.lean (ordinalMap_coefficient/coordinate/generator, substitute_*, coordinate_zero/succ, fiberValue). I did not check the other lemmas in the file for simp-normal-form problems beyond these. I can't run Lean, so the redundancy claim rests on reading the lemmas and the `by simp` proofs, not on a simpNF run. I found no cycles. The tail lemma suggestions are about convenience and consistency, and they carry some risk because the right-hand sides are `if` expressions.

findings.problem: homotopyMap_C and homotopyMap_X are tagged simp but are consequences of the simp rules already in place. Both have the form `homotopyMap n i (coefficient n _)`, which the simp lemma `homotopyMap_coefficient` already rewrites to `homotopyCoefficient n i _`. `homotopyCoefficient_C` and `homotopyCoefficient_X` then finish the job. Both lemmas are proved by a bare `simp`, which confirms this. So two simp rules compete with `homotopyMap_coefficient` on the same LHS, and their results are the same as the composite. This is redundant and would likely be flagged by simpNF. It also means the simp set has two routes to the same normal form for `homotopyMap`.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `homotopyMap_C` and `homotopyMap_X`. Keep them as plain theorems if they are wanted for `rw`, or delete them. The simp normal form then comes only from `homotopyMap_coefficient` followed by `homotopyCoefficient_C` and `homotopyCoefficient_X`. The `simp only [... homotopyMap_X ...]` calls in the face and degeneracy proofs can keep naming `homotopyMap_X` explicitly, since `simp only` does not need the simp attribute.
findings.benefit: The simp set has no overlapping rules on `homotopyMap n i (coefficient n _)`, and simp reaches one normal form by one route. A reader can see which lemma is canonical.

evidence.excerpt: homotopyMap n i (coefficient n p) = homotopyCoefficient n i p

findings.excerpt: theorem tail_zero (n : ℕ) : tail (R := R) n 0 = 1 := by
findings.problem: The tail API has no simp lemmas of its own, so every use has to name them by hand. `tail_zero` has no hypotheses and rewrites to the canonical value `1`. The sibling `coefficientMap_tail` is simp, so the `tail` interface is only partly set up. The shift lemmas `ordinalMap_tail_face` and `ordinalMap_tail_degeneracy` are passed explicitly to `simp` or `simp only` in about six face and degeneracy proofs. `tail_zero` and `tail_empty` are likewise passed by hand in `homotopyMap_face_zero` and `homotopyMap_face_last`, for example `simp [RingHom.comp_apply, ordinalMap_tail_face, tail_zero]`. The tail-pullback facts are therefore not found automatically, though the other `ordinalMap` rules (`ordinalMap_coefficient`, `ordinalMap_coordinate`) are simp.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `tail_zero` with `@[simp]`. It is unconditional, its RHS `1` is canonical, and it cannot loop. Consider tagging `ordinalMap_tail_face` and `ordinalMap_tail_degeneracy` as simp too, so that `ordinalMap (δ i) (tail (n+1) q)` normalizes to `tail n (if i.val < q then q-1 else q)`. The `if` on the RHS could make those two lemmas unwelcome in other contexts. If so, leave them as named lemmas and use the local `simp [..]` calls as they are, adding only `tail_zero`. `tail_empty` has a hypothesis `n < q`, which simp can discharge by `omega`-style arithmetic only sometimes, so leave it unannotated.
findings.benefit: Downstream proofs about homotopy faces, degeneracies and naturality would not need to list the tail lemmas by hand. The `tail` simp interface would be consistent with `coefficientMap_tail`.
